description:
Split from op-9c2e (GitHub issue #30, first comment: 'For tables it's the same, draw box, right click, digitise with OCR, check values then option to export csv or copy/paste'). Depends on op-6ez3 (needs a rendered page region to OCR against).

TENSION TO RESOLVE EXPLICITLY: this workspace's KOVAN design principles (docs/kovan.md 'Deterministic First') and the root CLAUDE.md's graph-digitiser rule both lean hard offline-deterministic/no-ML ('there is no tick-label OCR (no ML, per KOVAN's offline-deterministic rule)' -- root CLAUDE.md, 'Graph digitisation' section). Table OCR is explicitly what that rule has so far excluded from the plot digitiser. The maintainer is now asking for it for TABLES specifically, which is new ground for this crate and needs an explicit decision, not a silent exception.

WHAT NEEDS DECIDING:
- OCR engine choice: candidates include Tesseract (via a Rust binding -- C dependency, licensing to check, Android/Termux story), or an offline Rust-native OCR (maturity/accuracy trade-off), or deferring pending a cloud/API choice explicitly ruled out by this crate's local-first principle unless the maintainer says otherwise.
- Whether/how this fits 'Deterministic First' -- OCR output is inherently probabilistic/model-dependent in a way the rest of KOVAN is not; the maintainer's own spec already anticipates this with 'digitise with OCR, CHECK VALUES then option to export' -- i.e. human review is mandatory before export, matching the existing digitiser's UNREVIEWED/reviewed pattern (crates/kovan-literature/src/digitiser/dataset.rs).
- Android/Termux impact -- does the OCR dependency get feature-gated off Android like eframe/egui already are, per the workspace's Android hard rule.

DELIVERABLE: a written recommendation for the maintainer, not code. Blocks the table-digitiser implementation bead until approved.
title: kovan: DECISION -- OCR tooling/policy for table digitisation

description: Graded refinement: refine the carve's boundary-adjacent cells one level finer, keeping the mesh conforming by SPLITTING the coarse transition cell's face into the 4 fine sub-faces (hanging nodes) -> the coarse cell becomes polyhedral (>6 faces). v1: single-level near-boundary refinement (auto 2:1-balanced); multi-level + full balancing is future. Leaf model keyed by (level,i,j,k), points deduped by finest-resolution integer coord, emission rule 'finer side owns the split faces'. New octree module: refine_near_boundary(points,tris,base_cell_size). V&V: a box refined near its walls keeps EXACT box volume, validate() closed (incl polyhedral coarse cells), cell count grows, and some cell has >6 faces (a polyhedral transition cell).
title: cfmesh: octree near-wall refinement (hanging-node face splitting -> polyhedral cells)

description:
The virtual-lattice port (src/geometry/virtual_lattice/) is currently a STANDALONE data structure: it builds, traverses and locates correctly, but nothing in the transport path calls it. Cell::distance_to_boundary still scans every surface in the region.

Upstream wires it at three points (vendored fork, commit be04e28):
  - src/cell.cpp:631  CSGCell::distance() branches to distance_in_virtual_lattice when the cell carries the virtual_lattice flag
  - src/universe.cpp:42  Universe::find_cell() branches to find_cell_in_virtual_lattice when filled_with_triso_base_ != -1
  - src/geometry.cpp:299  find_cell_in_virtual_lattice handles the coord-level/material bookkeeping

The third is deep OpenMC model:: global machinery (coord levels, distribcell, sqrtkT) and was deliberately NOT ported — it needs a decision about how our Geometry/Universe types carry the equivalent state.

Scope: add an optional virtual lattice to Cell, branch distance_to_boundary onto it, and decide the Universe-level story. Until this lands the port is dead code in the transport sense — see the workspace 'no orphaned dead code' rule.

NOTE: not ported and probably not wanted — the XML (pugixml) input parsing for the virtual_lattice/lower_left/pitch/shape/triso_particle nodes, and the openmc/cell.py + openmc/model/triso.py Python API. XML parsing is explicitly out of scope for this crate.
title: Wire VirtualLattice into Cell/Universe so transport actually uses it

description: CIET Educational Simulator v2 as a BINARY in outram-park-digital-twin-engine (v1 is an example in tuas and stays untouched). Hosts an OPC-UA server on a parallel thread; clients write controls (heater power, CTAH pump pressure, CTAH/TCHX outlet set points, frequency-response settings, branch blocking) and read outputs (heater power, key BT temperatures, FM flowrates, sim time). UI shows the endpoint URL + node table so a user knows how to connect. Binds 127.0.0.1 by default, --bind opts into LAN. Must compile for aarch64-linux-android and degrade gracefully on Termux (headless: physics + OPC-UA, no egui).
title: CIET Educational Simulator v2 + OPC-UA server

description: Ensure egui/eframe/windowing stays in examples / optional bins / feature-gated code, never in a crate's unconditional lib build, so libraries build headless for Android. Audit tampines-steam-tables and boon-lay (which have egui example apps) and any crate with a [[bin]] pulling GUI.
title: Keep GUI (egui/eframe) out of unconditional library builds
